edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: adults with type 2 diabetes or heart failure
edges.mechanism: By causing glycosuria, natriuresis, and mild osmotic diuresis, SGLT2 inhibitors unload the heart and reduce congestion while also shifting myocardial fuel use toward ketones, a plausible route to fewer heart-failure events.
edges.summary: What makes this pair believable is not one flashy paper but the way the literature stacks up: the 2026 Bodea meta analysis in J Clin Med already points to sglt2 inhibitors tracks with lower risk or better outcomes, and later studies mostly refine the size of the effect rather than overturning it. In practice this reads more like a real risk signal than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
